body.objective: Make the normal Science Forge lease path fast and comfortable at programme scale. A single `s-f work assign` on the live physics corpus consumed roughly 90 seconds of one CPU before writing a correct lease, even though the read-only overview fold is now only a few seconds. Pull, assign, renew, yield, abort and close are inner-loop coordination operations and must not rescan or refold the entire append-only corpus expensively on every mutation.
body.stop_condition: Profile the live-sized path and identify the time spent in event discovery, JSON parsing, lifecycle folding, dependency folding, effective-scope calculation, active-overlap CAS and Git state checks. Introduce a content-addressed incremental fold/index or equivalent bounded mutation path whose cache key includes every authoritative work item and event input. Preserve a full-fold fallback and verify cached == uncached state byte-for-byte. On a deterministic fixture at least as large as the current physics programme (>=4,000 events, >=135 open items, >=7 streams), warm `work assign`, `work pull`, `work renew` and `work yield` must each complete in under 1 second p95; a stale/missing-cache rebuild followed by the requested mutation must complete in under 4 seconds p95 on the reference machine. The final acquire guard must still recheck lifecycle, one-lease-per-agent, dependencies and active write-scope overlap atomically before writing an event. Add concurrent-writer, stale-cache, moved-HEAD, corrupt-cache, expired-lease and append-during-rebuild fixtures, with C == native and ASan-clean gates. If an operation exceeds two seconds, the wrapper must print a short progress reason rather than appearing hung. Document cache location, invalidation, rebuild and recovery in GUIDE.md and expose timing/cache-hit fields in an opt-in diagnostic mode.
body.forbid: no weakening or bypassing the final lease CAS; no cache treated as authoritative over append-only events; no wall-clock-only invalidation; no silently stale lifecycle or overlap decision; no global daemon required for correctness; no background mutation; no performance claim from a toy ten-event fixture; no hiding a slow rebuild without progress output; no change to scientific lifecycle semantics
notes: Live reproduction 2026-07-22: after a verified cross-stream request correctly changed programme-global-paper-coverage-baseline from BLOCKED to READY, `s-f work assign --item programme-global-paper-coverage-baseline --agent coordinator --now 2026-07-22T03:41:30Z --expires 2026-07-22T06:41:30Z` ran at approximately 100% CPU for about 90 seconds before landing the correct ACTIVE/LEASE events.
The same corpus currently contains 135 open work items across seven streams and more than two hundred terminal results. This is already normal operational scale, not an artificial stress test.

A correct slow lease path is safer than a fast incorrect one, but it is too costly for five resident agents that pull, report and release work repeatedly. The target is exact incremental state, not relaxed coordination discipline.
